chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In the last chapter, you and I started to step through the internal workings of a transformer.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This is one of the key pieces of technology inside large language models, and a lot of

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: other tools in the modern wave of AI.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: It first hit the scene in a now-famous 2017 paper called Attention is All You Need, and

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: in this chapter you and I will dig into what this attention mechanism is, visualizing how

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: it processes data.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As a quick recap, here's the important context I want you to have in mind.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The goal of the model you and I are studying is to take in a piece of text and predict

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: what word comes next.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The input text is broken up into little pieces that we call tokens, and these are very often

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: words or pieces of words, but just to make the examples in this video easier for you

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and me to think about, let's simplify by pretending that tokens are always just words.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The first step in a transformer is to associate each token with a high-dimensional vector,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: what we call its embedding.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The most important idea I want you to have in mind is how directions in this high-dimensional

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: space of all possible embeddings can correspond with semantic meaning.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In the last chapter we saw an example for how direction can correspond to gender, in

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the sense that adding a certain step in this space can take you from the embedding of a

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: masculine noun to the embedding of the corresponding feminine noun.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: That's just one example you could imagine how many other directions in this high-dimensional

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: space could correspond to numerous other aspects of a word's meaning.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The aim of a transformer is to progressively adjust these embeddings so that they don't

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: merely encode an individual word, but instead they bake in some much, much richer contextual

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: meaning.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: I should say up front that a lot of people find the attention mechanism, this key piece

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: in a transformer, very confusing, so don't worry if it takes some time for things to

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: sink in.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: I think that before we dive into the computational details and all the matrix multiplications,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: it's worth thinking about a couple examples for the kind of behavior we want attention

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to enable.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Consider the phrases American true mole, one mole of carbon dioxide, and take a biopsy

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of the mole.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: You and I know that the word mole has different meanings in each one of these, based on the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: context.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: But after the first step of a transformer, the one that breaks up the text and associates

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: each token with a vector, the vector associated with mole would be the same in all three of

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: these cases, because this initial token embedding is effectively a lookup table with no reference

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to the context.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: It's only in the next step of the transformer that the surrounding embeddings have the chance

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to pass information into this one.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The picture you might have in mind is that there are multiple distinct directions in

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: this embedding space encoding the multiple distinct meanings of the word mole, and that

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: a well-trained attention block calculates what you need to add to the generic embedding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to move it to one of these more specific directions, as a function of the context.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: To take another example, consider the embedding of the word tower.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This is presumably some very generic non-specific direction in the space, associated with lots

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of other large, tall nouns.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: If this word was immediately preceded by Eiffel, you could imagine wanting the mechanism to

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: update this vector so that it points in a direction that more specifically encodes the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Eiffel tower, maybe correlated with vectors associated with Paris and France and things

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: made of steel.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: If it was also preceded by the word miniature, then the vector should be updated even further

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: so that it no longer correlates with large, tall things.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: More generally than just refining the meaning of a word, the attention block allows the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: model to move information encoded in one embedding to that of another, potentially ones that

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: are quite far away, and potentially with information that's much richer than just

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: a single word.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: What we saw in the last chapter was how after all of the vectors flow through the network,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: including many different attention blocks, the computation you perform to produce a prediction

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of the next token is entirely a function of the last vector in the sequence.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So imagine for example that the text you input is most of an entire mystery novel, all the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: way up to a point near the end, which reads, therefore the murderer was.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: If the model is going to accurately predict the next word, that final vector in the sequence,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: which began its life simply embedding the word was, will have to have been updated by

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: all of the attention blocks to represent much more than any individual word, somehow encoding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: all of the information from the full context window that's relevant to predicting the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: next word.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: To step through the computations though, let's take a much simpler example.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Imagine that the input includes the phrase, a fluffy blue creature roamed the verdant

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: forest.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: And for the moment, suppose that the only type of update we care about is having the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: adjectives adjust the meanings of their corresponding nouns.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: What I'm about to describe is what we would call a single head of attention, and later

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: we will see how the attention block consists of many different heads run in parallel.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Again, the initial embedding for each word is some high dimensional vector that only

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: encodes the meaning of that particular word with no context.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Actually, that's not quite true.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: They also encode the position of the word.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: There's a lot more to say about the specific way the positions are encoded, but right now

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: all you need to know is that the entries of this vector are enough to tell you both what

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the word is and where it exists in the context.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Let's go ahead and denote these embeddings with the letter e.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The goal is to have a series of computations produce a new refined set of embeddings where

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: for example those corresponding to the nouns have ingested the meaning from their corresponding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: adjectives.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: And playing the deep learning game, we want most of the computations involved to look

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: like matrix vector products, where the matrices are full of tunable weights, things that the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: model will learn based on data.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: To be clear, I'm making up this example of adjectives updating nouns just to illustrate

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the type of behavior that you could imagine an attention head doing.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As with so much deep learning, the true behavior is much harder to parse, because it's based

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: on tweaking and tuning a huge number of parameters to minimize some cost function.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: It's just that as we step through all the different matrices filled with parameters

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: that are involved in this process, I think it's really helpful to have an imagined example

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of something that it could be doing to help keep it all more concrete.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For the first step of this process, you might imagine each noun, like a creature, asking

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the question, hey, are there any adjectives sitting in front of me?

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: And for the words fluffy and blue to each be able to answer, yeah, I'm an adjective,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and I'm in that position.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: That question is somehow encoded as yet another vector, another list of numbers, which we

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: call the query for this word.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This query vector, though, has a much smaller dimension than the embedding vector, say 128.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Computing this query looks like taking a certain matrix, which I'll label WQ, and multiplying

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: it by the embedding.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Let's write that query vector as Q, and then any time you see me put a matrix next to an

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: arrow like this one, it's meant to represent that multiplying this matrix by the vector

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: at the arrow's start gives you the vector at the arrow's end.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In this case, you multiply this matrix by all of the embeddings in the context, producing

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: one query vector for each token.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The entries of this matrix are parameters of the model, which means the true behavior

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: is learned from data, and in practice what this matrix does in a particular attention

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: head is challenging to parse.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: But for our sake, imagining an example that we might hope it would learn, we'll suppose

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: that this query matrix maps the embeddings of nouns to certain directions in this smaller

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: query space that somehow encodes the notion of looking for adjectives in preceding positions.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As to what it does to other embeddings, who knows, maybe it simultaneously tries to accomplish

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: some other goal with those, right now we're laser focused on the nouns.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: At the same time, associated with this is a second matrix, called the key matrix, which

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: you also multiply by every one of the embeddings.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This produces a second sequence of vectors that we call the keys.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Conceptually, you want to think of the keys as potentially answering the queries.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This key matrix is also full of tunable parameters, and just like the query matrix, it maps the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: embedding vectors to that same smaller dimensional space.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: You think of the keys as matching the queries whenever they closely align with each other.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In our example, you would imagine that the key matrix maps the adjectives, like fluffy

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and blue, to vectors that are closely aligned with the query produced by the word creature.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: To measure how well each key matches each query, you compute a dot product between each

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: possible key query pair.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: I like to visualize a grid full of a bunch of dots, where the bigger dots correspond

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to the larger dot products, the places where the keys and queries align.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For our adjective noun example, that would look a little more like this, where if the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: keys produced by fluffy and blue really do align closely with the query produced by creature,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: then the dot products in these two spots would be some large positive numbers.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In the lingo, machine learning people would say that this means the embeddings of fluffy

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and blue attend to the embedding of creature.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The contrast to the dot product between the key for some other word, like the, and the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: query for creature, would be some small or negative value that reflects that these are

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: unrelated to each other.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So we have this grid of values that can be any real number from negative infinity to

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: infinity, giving us a score for how relevant each word is to updating the meaning of every

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: other word.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The way we're about to use these scores is to take a certain weighted sum along each

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: column weighted by the relevance.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So instead of having values range from negative infinity to infinity, what we want is for

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the numbers in these columns to be between 0 and 1, and for each column to add up to

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: 1, as if they were a probability distribution.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: If you're coming in from the last chapter, you know what we need to do then.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: We compute a softmax along each one of these columns to normalize the values.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: In our picture, after you apply softmax to all of the columns, we'll fill in the grid

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: with these normalized values.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: At this point you're safe to think about each column as giving weights according to how

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: relevant the word on the left is to the corresponding value at the top.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: We call this grid an attention pattern.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Now if you look at the original transformer paper, there's a really compact way that they

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: write this all down.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Here the variables q and k represent the full arrays of query and key vectors respectively,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: those little vectors you get by multiplying the embeddings by the query and key matrices.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This expression up in the numerator is a really compact way to represent the grid of all possible

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: dot products between pairs of keys and queries.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: A small technical detail that I didn't mention is that for numerical stability, it happens

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to be helpful to divide all of these values by the square root of the dimension in that

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: key query space.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Then this softmax that's wrapped around the full expression is meant to be understood

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: to apply column by column.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As to that v term, we'll talk about it in just a second.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Before that, there's one other technical detail that so far I've skipped.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: During the training process, when you run this model on a given text example, and all

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of the weights are slightly adjusted and tuned to either reward or punish it based on how

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: high a probability it assigns to the true next word in the passage, it turns out to

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: make the whole training process a lot more efficient if you simultaneously have it predict

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: every possible next token following each initial subsequence of tokens in this passage.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For example, with the phrase we've been focusing on, it might also be predicting what

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: words follow creature, and what words follow the.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This is really nice, because it means what would otherwise be a single training example

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: effectively acts as many.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For the purposes of our attention pattern, it means that you never want to allow later

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: words to influence earlier words, since otherwise they could kind of give away the answer for

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: what comes next.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: What this means is that we want all of these spots here, the ones representing later tokens

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: influencing earlier ones, to somehow be forced to be 0.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The simplest thing you might think to do is to set them equal to 0, but if you did that,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: the columns wouldn't add up to 1 anymore, they wouldn't be normalized.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So instead, a common way to do this is that before applying softmax, you set all of those

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: entries to be negative infinity.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: If you do that, then after applying softmax, all of those get turned into 0, but the columns

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: stay normalized.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This process is called masking.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: There are versions of attention where you don't apply it, but in our GPT example, even

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: though this is more relevant during the training phase than it would be, say, running it as

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: a chatbot or something like that, you do always apply this masking to prevent later tokens

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: from influencing earlier ones.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Another fact that's worth reflecting on about this attention pattern is how its size

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: is equal to the square of the context size.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So this is why context size can be a really huge bottleneck for large language models,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and scaling it up is non-trivial.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As you might imagine, motivated by a desire for bigger and bigger context windows, recent

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: years have seen some variations to the attention mechanism aimed at making context more scalable,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: but right here, you and I are staying focused on the basics.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: OK, great, computing this pattern lets the model deduce which words are relevant to which

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: other words.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Now you need to actually update the embeddings, allowing words to pass information to whichever

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: other words they're relevant to.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For example, you want the embedding of fluffy to somehow cause a change to creature that

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: moves it to a different part of this 12,000 dimensional embedding space that more specifically

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: encodes a fluffy creature.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: What I'm going to do here is first show you the most straightforward way that you could

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: do this, though there's a slight way that this gets modified in the context of multi-headed

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: attention.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: This most straightforward way would be to use a third matrix, what we call the value

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: matrix, which you multiply by the embedding of that first word, for example fluffy.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: The result of this is what you would call a value vector, and this is something that

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: you add to the embedding of the second word, in this case something you add to the embedding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of creature.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: So this value vector lives in the same very high dimensional space as the embeddings.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: When you multiply this value matrix by the embedding of a word, you might think of it

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: as saying, if this word is relevant to adjusting the meaning of something else, what exactly

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: should be added to the embedding of that something else in order to reflect this?

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Looking back in our diagram, let's set aside all of the keys and the queries, since after

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: you compute the attention pattern you're done with those, then you're going to take

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: this value matrix and multiply it by every one of those embeddings to produce a sequence

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: of value vectors.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: You might think of these value vectors as being kind of associated with the corresponding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: keys.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For each column in this diagram, you multiply each of the value vectors by the corresponding

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: weight in that column.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: For example here, under the embedding of creature, you would be adding large proportions of the

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: value vectors for fluffy and blue, while all of the other value vectors get zeroed out,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: or at least nearly zeroed out.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: And then finally, the way to actually update the embedding associated with this column,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: previously encoding some context-free meaning of creature, you add together all of these

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: rescaled values in the column, producing a change that you want to add, that I'll label

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: delta e, and then you add that to the original embedding.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Hopefully what results is a more refined vector encoding the more contextually rich meaning,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: like that of a fluffy blue creature.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: And of course you don't just do this to one embedding, you apply the same weighted sum

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: across all of the columns in this picture, producing a sequence of changes.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Adding all of those changes to the corresponding embeddings produces a full sequence of more

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: refined embeddings popping out of the attention block.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: Zooming out, this whole process is what you would describe as a single head of attention.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: As I've described things so far, this process is parametrized by three distinct matrices,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: all filled with tunable parameters, the key, the query, and the value.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: I want to take a moment to continue what we started in the last chapter with a scorekeeping

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: where we count up the total number of model parameters using the numbers from GPT-3.

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: These key and query matrices each have 12,288 columns, matching the embedding dimension,

chunks.title: Attention in transformers
chunks.text: and 128 rows, matching the dimension of that smaller key query space.
